checks.evidence: _nonempty_strings and the placeholder scan use pd.unique on object values. Results: a single-category categorical is publishable, with no TypeError (G7 fixed). An unused category 'nan' is ignored, because only present values count. A categorical holding an NA value is invalid_identity. A present categorical value 'nan' is invalid and the affected subject is named. All four identity columns categorical: 3 of 3 eligible. pyarrow-backed string dtype is publishable. FutureWarning promoted to error raised nothing.

Two observations, one with source_recording_id AB01/NaN/2. The bad observation gets invalid_identity with its identity and a message quoting the value. A file-level placeholder_identity_in_file issue makes both observations invalid and not eligible; the good one carries only the file-level reason, so fail-closed is preserved. Defect: affected = sum(issue.code == 'invalid_identity' ...) counts issues, not observations. One observation with subject 'nan' and source_recording_id 'AB01/nan' produces the message '2 observation(s) have placeholder identities' when only one observation is affected.

assess_observations orders observations by first appearance for both the plain and categorical inputs: ['S2','S1','S3'] for subject categories [S3,S1,S2], and o1,o2,o3 for reversed observation_id categories. End-to-end release in the scratchpad (build_release, synthetic 3-observation fixture, legacy profile): the plain-string input and the categorical input with reverse-lexical categories in subject, source_recording_id and observation_id both give 450 filtered rows in the same observation order [o3, o2, o1]. _filtered_rows casts categorical identities to object before sorting, so the order is lexical either way. This covers the handoff's untested case.

These match the code: the side-none role sentence; 'any recorded clock value fails the contract'; the whole-value token list with case, full-width and zero-width folding; 'NA alone remains valid'; naming each affected observation, with no observation in the file eligible; categorical columns assessed like strings; 'earliest and latest values after sorting'. The mismatch: 'Neither is a composite ID with such a part' covers None, null and NaT parts, but _PLACEHOLDER_PARTS excludes them on purpose, and the text does not say which separators split a composite.

A reviewed profile without applicability returns ['level_walking']; after adding a population block it returns []. A legacy (unlabelled) profile returns []. An approved profile with an empty applicability {} returns ['level_walking']. The builder now enforces it (build_dataset_release.py lines 479-484).

required_fixes: F1 (data_contract.py): count distinct affected observation identities for placeholder_identity_in_file, not invalid_identity issues, so that one observation with placeholders in two columns reports 1. Add a fixture with two placeholder columns in one observation.

F2 (DATA_CONTRACT.md): state the composite rule exactly. Parts are split only on / \ : | ; , and a part fails only when it is one of nan, -nan, <NA>, <missing>, <undefined>, N/A, #N/A. None, null and NaT parts are accepted because they can be real labels. Parts joined by _, -, . or spaces are not split.
optional: Consider rejecting empty or blank composite parts (AB01//t1, AB01/ /t1). They are the typical result of formatting a missing string component, e.g. sprintf with an empty value, and no source identity needs an empty path segment.
Consider adding #NA and 1.#QNAN (spreadsheet and MSVC NaN spellings) to the token sets. Neither can be a real identity.
observations_not_blocking: By design, composites with None/null/NaT parts and identities joined by _, -, . or spaces are not inspected. This is a reasonable trade-off against false positives (nan_trial, NaT-7, AB01/none/t1), and it should be documented exactly (F2).
Homoglyph or soft-hyphen variants (na\u00adn) pass. They cannot come from stringification, so no action is needed.
The effect on existing converted exports is still unknown until a bounded pilot re-assessment runs under the guarded launcher (as stated in the handoff).
